answer: Sparrow-tag bandwidth titration. Each agent identity gets a routing slot keyed to a hardware-rooted radio fingerprint, and traffic is admitted through a fixed inlet sized to one device's measured throughput. The scheduler interleaves slots in a rotating spiral so a claimant must hold the channel continuously to keep standing. Faking N identities requires N physical radios transmitting in parallel, since relayed fingerprints collapse to the relay's capacity and lose their slots. Cost to attacker: one radio per identity plus idle power to keep each inlet open.
